messages.subject: Foraging and basking tables
messages.subject_clean: Foraging and basking tables
messages.body_plain:
Hi all, I was hoping someone could tell me if I’m
interpreting the graphs wrong?
When creating the basking and foraging table (as shown in the tutorial), there
are gaps in activity corresponding to months where the species temperature exceeds
T_F_max. However, this does not occur in January for any of the runs, in spite
of January having the highest temperatures (screenshot attached).

In addition, when I increase the level of shade, no time for
basking is required in winter months. The results above at 0% shade (5-10%
gives almost identical results). However, at 30% shade, my results are as
follows:

It seems illogical that greater shade means basking is no longer
required.

Thanks in advance if anyone has a spare second to look at this.

Cheers,
Alex

messages.subject: How to create future climate data for microclimate model from monthly temperature and pricipation and then load as new imput climate data?
messages.subject_clean: How to create future climate data for microclimate model from monthly temperature and pricipation and then load as new imput climate data?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael and all others,

Recently I run NicheMapR for several lizards distributed in China.

I found I can  use get.global.climate() function to obtain current climate easily and then run microclimate and  ectotherm model. But when I want to run models to simulate for climate change, it do not offer link directly in this package.

After reading some paper using NichemapR, I found I can download future climate data from other source (e.g. monthly maximum and mimimum temperature, precipitatin from WorldClim), and  compute predicted monthly differences(i.e.,offsets), then add the offsets to the baseline maximum and minimum temperatures and precipitation values.

My question is:
1.  How to load the new climate data into micro_global function() or microcliamte model?
2. The above method may be suitable for modeling several sites, how about regional scale? If still use above mothod for all girds, why not use the new monthly temperature and precipitation layers replace the baseline layers directly?
3. If can't replace, how can I generate my own future climate data in NicheMapR, when I only have the future monthly temperature and precipitation data from WorldClim, and how to load?

Look forward your reply and best wishes,

Mi

messages.subject_clean: Foraging and basking tables
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

I see that you are running the microclimate model for 10 years, but your plot is plotting all 10 years on one graph, overlapping the day of year for each year. Try just running one year and plotting and it should make more sense.

Also, re the 'basking' status - it is perhaps a bit misleading in that it is not the first stage in emergence necessarily. I put it there for a situation where the animal can come out from its retreat to be warmer than it would be in the retreat, despite it not being warm enough to forage. Many lizards do this on cool days and even during prolonged periods where activity isn't possible on the shoulder seasons. What they're doing is speeding up their metabolism, e.g. to drive growth or preparation for reproduction, drawing from their reserves. The model is a steady-state model so there is no basking from the point of view of waiting to warm up due to the lag of heating - they just instantly get to the steady state temperature. So that kind of basking isn't relevant.

Hope that clears things up.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: How to create future climate data for microclimate model from monthly temperature and pricipation and then load as new imput climate data?
messages.subject_clean: How to create future climate data for microclimate model from monthly temperature and pricipation and then load as new imput climate data?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Mi,

Sorry, there is not yet a pipeline for running the model under climate change scenarios. That is something for which you would need to modify the code yourself. You'd need to make your own version of micro_global, where you alter the monthly values extracted from the global climate database according to the scenario you're using, before they are passed to the microclimate model itself.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Operative temperature
messages.subject_clean: Operative temperature
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mi,

It's "TC". Operative temperature is the 'steady state' temperature some object would reach if held indefinitely in a given environment, and this is essentially what the model is predicting. It's the same as what you'd get with a low heat capacity physical model of the organism, e.g. one made of copper, so it changes temperature almost instantly as the environment changes (e.g. as the sun comes out from behind a cloud). I.e. it isn't accounting for the object lagging behind the temperature its environment is driving it towards, because of rapid changes in the environment. For many small organisms, and many questions, the steady state or operative temperatures provided by the 'ectotherm' model are fine. But if you want to account for the lag, then you can use the 'transient' models ('onelump', 'onelump_var' and 'twolump_var'), e.g. see http://bioforecasts.science.unimelb.edu.au/app_direct/ectotherm_transient/

All the best,

> Hi Mi,

messages.subject_clean: food density, and functional response in NicheMapR
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm using NicheMapR mainly to apply the DEB model to fish species in an aquaculture context.

In this context, the feed is distributed to the fish by the farmer. Depending on different factors, the daily quantity of feed distributed to the fish will vary.

I would like to know how can I estimate a daily food density (X) using data about the daily mass of feed distributed to the fish and it's energy content?

It may be necessary to note that in marine fish farming, the feed can sink through the cage, and thus the fish only have access to food for a limited time.

In NicheMapR we can force (X), to I guess that the functional response (f) is calculated automatically using the relation f = X/(X+K). Is it possible to see what is the f value calculated in NicheMapR for an X value?

Also, the new parameter Esm (maximum specific stomach energy) was introduced in NicheMapR, but values are not given in Add my pet for this parameter. How can I estimate Esm?

Thanks for your ideas,
Best regards,
Killian

messages.subject: Re: food density, and functional response in NicheMapR
messages.subject_clean: food density, and functional response in NicheMapR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Killian,

Because NicheMapR is aimed at simulating an animal on an hourly time-step, capturing constraints on activity, I added in the stomach. Otherwise no assimilation would be happening e.g. overnight. I made it so that the assimilation rate p_A goes to zero when the stomach is empty, and food density affects the stomach dynamics via the equation (taken from the DEB_euler function):

      J_X <- F_mT * ((X / K) / (1 + X / K)) * V ^ (2 / 3)
      dEsdt <- J_X * f - (p_AmT / kap_X) * V ^ (2 / 3)

so 'f' is sitting there as an independent override on what is happening in terms of food dynamics affecting stomach dynamics but there's a hidden/implied f in the J_X function above. So it isn't very straightforward to estimate food density via NicheMapR.

Re the stomach energy density, you could work it out with observations of stomach energy contents for an individual of known structural volume. You can see how I made an estimate for the Australian sleepy lizard in:
Kearney, M.R., Munns, S.L., Moore, D., Malishev, M. & Bull, C.M. (2018) Field tests of a general ectotherm niche model show how water can limit lizard activity and distribution. Ecological Monographs, 88, 672–693.

Hope that helps,

All the best,
Mike

messages.body_plain:
Hi Julie,

As the comments in the code mention, the first two lines are just making string variables that are to be used as file names. The next line creates a new ncdf file with '_time2.nc <http://time2.nc>' in the name. The line after that is putting data into that file, then it is closed and the line creating the 'cmd' variable is putting together what you'd type into the console to run ncpdq, where it is given a file name to rearrange (the '_time2.nc <http://time2.nc>' file) and a file to write the rearrangement to (a file ending with '_time.nc <http://time.nc>'). The 'system(cmd)' line runs ncpdq from R but it is the same as typing the text in 'cmd' into the console of your operating system. If you never see the file ending with '_time.nc <http://time.nc>' then it appears that 'system(cmd)' isn't working, I suspect because you haven't got ncpdq running properly.

Hope that helps,

Mike

> I will check your publication regarding the stomach energy density. Thanks !
>
> All the best,
> Killian
>
>
> Le vendredi 25 septembre 2020 à 14:30:03 UTC+2, Michael Kearney a écrit :
> > Hi Killian,
> >
> > Because NicheMapR is aimed at simulating an animal on an hourly time-step, capturing constraints on activity, I added in the stomach. Otherwise no assimilation would be happening e.g. overnight. I made it so that the assimilation rate p_A goes to zero when the stomach is empty, and food density affects the stomach dynamics via the equation (taken from the DEB_euler function):
> >
> >       J_X <- F_mT * ((X / K) / (1 + X / K)) * V ^ (2 / 3)
> >       dEsdt <- J_X * f - (p_AmT / kap_X) * V ^ (2 / 3)
> >
> > so 'f' is sitting there as an independent override on what is happening in terms of food dynamics affecting stomach dynamics but there's a hidden/implied f in the J_X function above. So it isn't very straightforward to estimate food density via NicheMapR.
> >
> > Re the stomach energy density, you could work it out with observations of stomach energy contents for an individual of known structural volume. You can see how I made an estimate for the Australian sleepy lizard in:
> > Kearney, M.R., Munns, S.L., Moore, D., Malishev, M. & Bull, C.M. (2018) Field tests of a general ectotherm niche model show how water can limit lizard activity and distribution. Ecological Monographs, 88, 672–693.
> >
> > Hope that helps,
> >
> > All the best,
> > Mike

> > > I'm using NicheMapR mainly to apply the DEB model to fish species in an aquaculture context.

> > > I would like to know how can I estimate a daily food density (X) using data about the daily mass of feed distributed to the fish and it's energy content?

> > > It may be necessary to note that in marine fish farming, the feed can sink through the cage, and thus the fish only have access to food for a limited time.
> > >
> > > In NicheMapR we can force (X), to I guess that the functional response (f) is calculated automatically using the relation f = X/(X+K). Is it possible to see what is the f value calculated in NicheMapR for an X value?
> > >
> > > Also, the new parameter Esm (maximum specific stomach energy) was introduced in NicheMapR, but values are not given in Add my pet for this parameter. How can I estimate Esm?
> > >
> > > Thanks for your ideas,
> > > Best regards,
> > > Killian

messages.body_snippet:
Hi Killan,

Yes increasing X until you find that there are no more changes in growth predictions is showing you when feeding has become ad libitum and is limited by 'handling', not by encounter rate.

messages.subject: Re: Clarification of Leaf Area Indicies and change through time (mico_ncep)
messages.subject_clean: Clarification of Leaf Area Indicies and change through time (mico_ncep)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

I agree it is confusing that they have different defaults. I made it zero for microclima, because it uses lai to compute radiation hitting the ground and by default minimum shade is zero so you want lai to match that. The other lai is used in soil moisture calculations to partition the transpiration and evaporation in terms of whole-profile soil moisture, so they are doing different things. Note that you can pass a vector of daily values to the (non-microclima) lai input, to capture temporal changes. I've now made this clear in the help. You could pass a vector to the microclima lai input too but the microclima calculations just use the mean of these in the end.

All the best,
Mike
